title: Outboard Flap Track Fairing Attachment Rib Reinforcement at Track 3

ata.title: Wing Trailing Edge — Flap Support Structure

abstract: Reinforcement of the rib that carries the outboard flap track fairing at track 3, after aerodynamic buffet in the flap-extended condition produced fastener hole elongation on high-cycle aircraft.

sections.reason: Detailed visual inspections at the 12-year check found elongated fastener holes in the fairing attachment rib at outboard flap track 3 on nine aircraft, all of them operating a high proportion of short sectors. The driver is buffet excitation of the fairing trailing section in the approach flap configuration, which the original substantiation treated as a static case. No fairing has been lost and no crack has been found in the rib web, but the hole elongation reduces the residual bearing margin and, once past 0.6 mm, no repair scheme is available.
sections.description: The lower rib assembly D5730125554505 at outboard track 3 is replaced by an item with a thicker attachment flange and an increased fastener edge distance. A new sub-assembly cleat D5730125388807 is added between the rib and the rear spar cap RO324593-41 to shorten the free length of the fairing attachment and raise its first bending mode above the buffet band. The left-hand cleat BRDE298405-27 is retained but is re-drilled to the new pattern. Protective sleeving EN479208-64 is fitted where the fairing control rod passes the new cleat. The sensor target for flap position sensing, FIN 4982VU, is repositioned by 18 mm inboard so that its clearance to the new cleat is maintained through the full flap travel; the sensor itself is unchanged. Work is done with the fairing removed, in zones 562, 564 and 662. Revised detail is on drawing D57301231033.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 9.2 kg per aircraft, symmetric about the centre line. No electrical load change. The reinforced rib is not interchangeable with the original because the fastener pattern differs and the cleat cannot be installed on the original rib. The repeat detailed visual inspection of the fairing attachment is replaced by a general visual inspection at a longer interval. Flap position rigging values are unchanged, but the rigging task must reference the new sensor target position, so maintenance manual content for flap position sensing requires update.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN T00142 in August 2018 and available in service through a retrofit service bulletin. Embodiment takes about four days per wing with the flap in the extended position; the flap itself does not have to be removed.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN T00142 within the existing trailing edge build sequence
